Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CombatServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_combat_friendly_fire_disabled.gd

For the same runtime combat state and target conditions, MG tower firing cadence remains deterministic and is driven by runtime combat or building combat data rather than ad hoc scene behavior. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CombatServiceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Services/BuildingPlacementValidationTests.cs

When no hostile target is inside MG tower range, the tower stays armed and idle and does not emit false fire, hit, or damage feedback events. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_hud_updates_on_events.gd Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_hud_scene.gd

MG tower combat outcomes are resolved through the existing combat services, while Godot-side runtime behavior is limited to activation and combat feedback binding; acceptance fails if scene-side logic can make the tower appear active without shared-query attack resolution and combat-service damage dispatch occurring. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CombatServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_hud_updates_on_events.gd
test_strategy: xUnit: validate MG tower attack cadence, hostile-only filtering, and deterministic damage dispatch in Game.Core tests.
GdUnit4: verify placed MG towers auto-acquire targets, emit combat feedback, and preserve friendly-fire disablement in runtime scenes.
Acceptance refs/anchors gate: keep Task 48 tower-combat refs synchronized before review pipeline.

title: Spawn Barracks Units Into Battlefield Runtime
description: Promote barracks queue completion into live battlefield unit spawning with stats and ownership, while runtime-visible HUD outcome state stays synchronized via existing tech/resource contracts.
acceptance: No battlefield unit is spawned before a barracks job reaches deterministic completion, and each completed job results in a deployed battlefield combat unit rather than ending as queue-only bookkeeping. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/BarracksTrainingQueueTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_barracks_training_queue_flow.gd

The deployed unit uses the tech-modified stat snapshot captured for the completed barracks job, and the unit's runtime combat stats match that deterministic completion snapshot. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/BarracksUnitStatApplicationTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/State/TechRuntimeSnapshotTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_barracks_tech_snapshot_flow.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_barracks_techtree_stats.gd

Resource deductions, refunds, and barracks queue-state transitions remain deterministic across deployment, cancellation, and tech-change flows, and unit deployment stays consistent with the existing resource contracts. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/BarracksTrainingQueueTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_barracks_training_queue_flow.gd

Queue progression, resource accounting, and stat application are produced only by Game.Core deterministic contracts; Game.Godot may instantiate and owner-bind actors from completion outputs only and must not recompute barracks completion semantics. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/BarracksTrainingQueueTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_barracks_training_queue_flow.gd Game.Core.Tests/State/TechRuntimeSnapshotTests.cs

HUD-visible barracks outcome state must stay synchronized with existing tech/resource runtime contracts: successful completion surfaces deployment feedback with active unit presence, while failed deployment surfaces failure feedback without adding an active unit entry. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_barracks_training_queue_flow.gd Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_hud_updates_on_events.gd

Queue completion outputs stay semantically equivalent across Core and Godot boundaries: completion payload fields (owner binding, deployment outcome, and resource trace) are consumed by bridge/runtime without recomputation or field substitution. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/BarracksTrainingQueueTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_barracks_training_queue_flow.gd

Each completed barracks job registers its deployed unit into the active battle loop, and acceptance fails if a spawned actor does not participate in runtime combat. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/BarracksTrainingQueueTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_barracks_training_queue_flow.gd

Each deployed unit is bound to the correct owner or faction at spawn time, and acceptance fails if ownership is missing or assigned incorrectly after deployment. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/BarracksTrainingQueueTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_barracks_training_queue_flow.gd

When a barracks job reaches deterministic completion, deployment outcome is atomic at the registration boundary: completed_units is emitted only when an owner-bound combat unit is registered into the active battle loop; otherwise failed_deployments records the failure and no active battle unit is registered. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/BarracksTrainingQueueTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_barracks_training_queue_flow.gd

Game.Godot presents projectile launch, visible flight, impact, and cleanup only for combat outcomes that actually resolve, and timed-out or invalid projectiles are removed deterministically instead of persisting. title: Area Damage Resolver And Elite Pressure Slice
description: Add deterministic area-damage resolution and elite-pressure differentiation so combat pressure is not limited to flat single-target exchanges.
acceptance: Given identical combat inputs, an AoE-capable hit resolves in deterministic core services using config-backed radius, clamp, and mandatory falloff, and when no AoE-capable source is active the same flow resolves as single-target damage only. Acceptance fails if any AoE rule is skipped, optionalized, or resolved outside core. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CombatServiceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Domain/GameConfigTests.cs

Elite and boss enemies produce higher normalized runtime pressure and materially different combat outcomes than normal enemies, so wave pressure and encounter behavior remain distinguishable instead of collapsing into uniform fodder exchanges. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/WaveManagerBudgetChannelTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_hud_updates_on_events.gd

With friendly fire disabled, splash resolution applies damage only to valid hostile targets selected by the shared combat rules and leaves non-hostile or otherwise invalid targets unchanged. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CombatServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_combat_friendly_fire_disabled.gd

Elite and boss pressure values are derived from enemy config together with pressure-normalization config, and acceptance fails if runtime pressure differentiation is not produced from those config-backed inputs. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Domain/GameConfigTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Services/WaveManagerBudgetChannelTests.cs

Runtime scenes expose resolved splash results and elite-pressure differences during clustered or blocked-route combat, so the player can observe the combat and pressure outcome directly rather than infer hidden or ambiguous behavior. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_enemy_ai_blocked_route_fallback.gd Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_hud_updates_on_events.gd

With identical inputs and config, core-resolved splash damage outputs and runtime wave-pressure outputs stay source-consistent across repeated runs; acceptance fails if pressure or UI differentiation appears without matching deterministic core combat resolution. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CombatServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_enemy_ai_blocked_route_fallback.gd Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_hud_updates_on_events.gd

Scene adapters only forward hit data and present returned results; acceptance fails if AoE or elite-pressure resolution occurs outside deterministic core services. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CombatServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_hud_updates_on_events.gd

When no AoE-capable source and no elite-pressure trigger are active, combat remains in the baseline state with single-target damage only and baseline pressure readouts only. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CombatServiceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Domain/GameConfigTests.cs

When AoE or elite/boss differentiation is configured as visible, acceptance fails if runtime scenes show differentiation that is not backed by deterministic core-resolved combat and pressure outputs (no UI-only or adapter-only differentiation). Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/CombatServiceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_hud_updates_on_events.gd

When enemies cluster or routes are blocked, splash resolution changes observable hit distribution, kill efficiency, or exposure risk relative to single-target attacks; acceptance fails if splash only adds feedback without creating a gameplay-relevant spacing or risk-management difference. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_enemy_ai_blocked_route_fallback.gd Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_hud_updates_on_events.gd

GdUnit verifies that elite-pressure slices and splash outcomes remain observable and deterministic across repeated runtime-scene executions with identical inputs; acceptance fails if the same scene inputs produce drifting pressure readouts, inconsistent splash results, or divergent pressure-versus-combat conclusions. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Scenes/Combat/test_enemy_ai_blocked_route_fallback.gd Tests.Godot/tests/UI/test_hud_updates_on_events.gd
test_strategy: xUnit: validate AoE radius, clamp, and elite-pressure normalization rules in Game.Core tests.
GdUnit4: verify elite or boss pressure slices and AoE combat outcomes remain observable and deterministic in runtime scenes.
Acceptance refs/anchors gate: keep Task 51 elite-pressure refs synchronized before review pipeline.

title: Combat Lifecycle And Pooling Hardening
description: Stabilize combat object lifecycle, cleanup, and pooling so repeated waves do not leak nodes, references, or performance budget.
acceptance: During repeated spawn, death, and timeout churn, every dead actor, spent projectile, and timed-out transient combat effect is retired on the first cleanup pass, later cleanup sweeps are no-ops, and acceptance fails if any orphaned runtime actor remains live after retirement. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_perf_stress_endurance_presets.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_enemy_ai_blocked_map_fallback_timeout.gd

Across repeated combat churn, cleanup and pooling release stale lifecycle references, including shared registry handoff points, so reused runtime objects do not restore prior targets, keep retired links, or produce duplicate impacts. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/PerformanceBaselineVarianceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_combat_friendly_fire_disabled.gd

Across repeated combat churn, the hardened lifecycle path stays within the declared performance gates, and acceptance fails if cleanup or pooling changes introduce avoidable frame-time or endurance regressions. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/FrameTimeHotspotRankingTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_perf_stress_endurance_presets.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_perf_gate_thresholds_fixed_seed.gd

Blocked-map, death, and timeout scenarios retire the affected actors and transient effects and clear stale runtime references, and acceptance fails if the retirement pass leaves stuck combat state, registry leftovers, or live runtime remnants. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_enemy_ai_blocked_map_fallback_timeout.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_perf_gate_thresholds_fixed_seed.gd

Task 52 is accepted only when xUnit verifies shared lifecycle cleanup and stale-reference release rules and GdUnit verifies repeated wave churn behavior on the Windows Godot plus C# baseline; missing either test layer fails acceptance. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/FrameTimeHotspotRankingTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_perf_stress_endurance_presets.gd

Deterministic retirement rules for units, enemies, projectiles, and transient combat effects are defined in shared services, and acceptance fails if those rules exist only in adapters or node-local code. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/PerformanceBaselineVarianceTests.cs Game.Core.Tests/Services/FrameTimeHotspotRankingTests.cs

Adapters choose whether each retired runtime node is freed immediately or returned to a safe pool, and acceptance fails if shared services directly own node-free or pool-management behavior. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_perf_stress_endurance_presets.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_enemy_ai_blocked_map_fallback_timeout.gd

When no spent projectile, dead actor, or timed-out combat effect is pending cleanup, running the lifecycle sweep leaves combat state unchanged and performs no additional retirement work. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/PerformanceBaselineVarianceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_perf_gate_thresholds_fixed_seed.gd

Every retirement path routes retired runtime nodes through the adapter-owned queue_free or QueueFree path or a safe pool return path, and acceptance fails if any path bypasses that routing. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_perf_stress_endurance_presets.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_enemy_ai_blocked_map_fallback_timeout.gd

Lifecycle hardening integrates with the shared registry lifecycle path from Task 47, and acceptance fails if retirement bypasses registry release sequencing or leaves registry-held stale references after cleanup. Refs: Game.Core.Tests/Services/PerformanceBaselineVarianceTests.cs Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_enemy_ai_blocked_map_fallback_timeout.gd
test_strategy: xUnit: validate lifecycle cleanup, stale-reference release, and deterministic actor retirement in Game.Core tests.
GdUnit4: verify repeated spawn, death, projectile, and timeout churn stay within runtime cleanup and performance expectations.
Acceptance refs/anchors gate: keep Task 52 lifecycle-hardening refs synchronized before review pipeline.

title: Introduce The Stable Battle Screen Frame
description: Introduce the stable BattleMapScreen three-band frame while preserving existing HUD and navigation ownership.
acceptance: Entering BattleMapScreen via the existing ScreenNavigator route always renders one stable 1440 x 900 three-band frame (top, battlefield, bottom) and preserves that composition across re-entry and viewport resize; on narrower displays, only battlefield content can move horizontally while top and bottom bands keep constant horizontal position. Refs: Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_battle_map_screen_runtime_flow.gd Tests.Godot/tests/Integration/test_screen_navigation_flow.gd
